name: Escherichia coli
significance: First isolated from infant feces; became the most studied model organism in molecular biology.

name: Staphylococcus aureus
significance: Identified in surgical abscess pus, linking bacteria directly to suppuration.

name: Streptococcus pyogenes
significance: Named and characterized as the agent of erysipelas and wound infections.

name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
significance: Announcement fulfilled Koch's postulates and founded modern medical bacteriology.

name: Vibrio cholerae
significance: First described the comma-shaped bacillus in cholera victims; confirmed as causal agent by Koch in 1883.

name: Bacillus anthracis
significance: First bacterium ever proven to cause a specific disease, establishing germ theory experimentally.

name: Yersinia pestis
significance: Isolated during the Third Plague Pandemic, identifying the agent of bubonic plague.

name: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi
significance: Eberth observed the bacillus in typhoid tissue; Gaffky obtained pure culture in 1884.

name: Clostridium tetani
significance: First pure culture of the tetanus bacillus, enabling toxin and antitoxin research.

name: Clostridium botulinum
significance: Isolated after a fatal ham-related outbreak, identifying the source of botulism.

name: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
significance: Loeffler cultured the bacillus described by Klebs, later leading to the diphtheria antitoxin.

name: Bordetella pertussis
significance: Isolated the whooping cough bacillus, later used to develop the pertussis vaccine.

name: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
significance: First identification of gonococcus, linking a specific bacterium to a sexually transmitted disease.

name: Treponema pallidum
significance: Identified the spirochete responsible for syphilis using dark-field microscopy.

name: Helicobacter pylori
significance: Overturned the belief that ulcers were caused by stress; Marshall famously self-ingested the bacterium to prove causation.

name: Legionella pneumophila
significance: Isolated after the 1976 Philadelphia American Legion convention outbreak.

name: Listeria monocytogenes
significance: Described in an epidemic among laboratory rabbits and guinea pigs.

name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
significance: Isolated from blue-green wound discharge ("pyocyanin"), the pigment that gives it its name.

name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
significance: Identified as a cause of severe bacterial pneumonia, initially called Friedländer's bacillus.

name: Proteus mirabilis
significance: Named for its shape-shifting swarming colonies, after the Greek god Proteus.

name: Shigella dysenteriae
significance: Identified during a major dysentery epidemic in Japan.

name: Campylobacter jejuni
significance: Development of selective culture media revealed it as a leading cause of bacterial diarrheal illness.

name: Borrelia burgdorferi
significance: Isolated from ticks, identifying the spirochete responsible for Lyme disease.

name: Leptospira interrogans
significance: Identified as the cause of Weil's disease during a study of infected mine workers.

name: Francisella tularensis
significance: Isolated in Tulare County, California, during a plague-like illness in ground squirrels.

name: Brucella melitensis
significance: Identified as the cause of Malta fever among British garrison troops.

name: Mycobacterium leprae
significance: First bacterium ever linked to a human disease, predating Koch's postulates.

name: Rickettsia prowazekii
discoverer: Stanislaus von Prowazek; Henrique da Rocha Lima
significance: Identified as the agent of epidemic typhus; named posthumously for von Prowazek, who died of the disease.

name: Chlamydia trachomatis
significance: Observed characteristic inclusion bodies in trachoma-infected eye tissue.

name: Streptococcus pneumoniae
significance: Independently isolated by Pasteur and Sternberg from saliva, later identified as the leading cause of bacterial pneumonia.

name: Enterococcus faecalis
significance: First described as a distinct intestinal coccus, later reclassified out of genus Streptococcus in 1984.

name: Bacillus subtilis
significance: Cohn's description helped found bacterial taxonomy and the study of endospores.

name: Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus
significance: Isolated from traditional Bulgarian yogurt, later studied by Élie Metchnikoff for its link to longevity.

name: Streptomyces griseus
significance: Source of streptomycin, the first effective antibiotic treatment for tuberculosis.

name: Rhizobium leguminosarum
significance: First isolation of a nitrogen-fixing root-nodule bacterium, founding soil microbiology.

name: Nitrosomonas europaea
significance: Central organism in Winogradsky's discovery of chemolithotrophy and the nitrogen cycle.

name: Thiobacillus thioparus
significance: Demonstrated that bacteria could derive energy purely from oxidizing sulfur compounds.

name: Deinococcus radiodurans
significance: Isolated from canned meat that had been sterilized by gamma radiation, revealing extreme radiation resistance.

name: Thermus aquaticus
significance: Its heat-stable Taq polymerase later became essential to the PCR method.

name: Fusobacterium nucleatum
significance: Characterized as a key organism in the polymicrobial ecology of the human mouth.

name: Porphyromonas gingivalis
significance: Reclassified into its own genus after study as a principal pathogen in periodontal disease.

name: Bacteroides fragilis
significance: One of the first anaerobic gut bacteria characterized, now known as a dominant human gut symbiont.

name: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
significance: Became the first photosynthetic organism to have its full genome sequenced, in 1996.

name: Anabaena sp.
significance: Model organism for the study of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts in filamentous cyanobacteria.

name: Gloeobacter violaceus
significance: Lacks internal thylakoid membranes, making it a key organism for studying the evolution of photosynthesis.

name: Halobacterium salinarum
significance: One of the first archaea studied; its light-driven proton pump bacteriorhodopsin became a landmark discovery.

name: Sulfolobus acidocaldarius
significance: Isolated from acidic hot springs, expanding known limits of life to extreme heat and acidity.

name: Methanocaldococcus jannaschii
significance: First archaeal genome ever fully sequenced, in 1996, revealing archaea as a distinct domain of life.

name: Pyrococcus furiosus
significance: Hyperthermophile growing optimally near 100C, later a source of heat-stable Pfu DNA polymerase.

name: Nanoarchaeum equitans
significance: An obligate symbiont so minimal it founded an entirely new archaeal phylum.

name: Methanobrevibacter smithii
significance: The dominant archaeon of the human gut microbiome, involved in hydrogen removal during digestion.

name: Thermococcus kodakarensis
significance: Became a key genetic model organism for studying archaeal DNA replication and repair.

name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
significance: Pasteur's studies of its fermentation proved microorganisms, not spontaneous chemistry, cause fermentation.

name: Penicillium notatum
significance: Its accidental contamination of a bacterial culture led to the discovery of penicillin.

name: Candida albicans
significance: First fungal pathogen observed in a human patient (thrush), decades before germ theory was established.

name: Aspergillus niger
significance: Among the earliest fungi formally described; later became a workhorse for industrial citric acid production.

name: Aspergillus fumigatus
significance: Identified as a cause of lung disease in birds, later recognized as a major human respiratory pathogen.

name: Cryptococcus neoformans
significance: First described from a human bone lesion, later recognized as a major cause of fungal meningitis.

name: Trichophyton rubrum
significance: Characterized by Sabouraud, the founder of medical mycology, as a major cause of ringworm.

name: Histoplasma capsulatum
significance: Initially misidentified as a protozoan parasite in autopsy tissue before being recognized as a fungus.

name: Coccidioides immitis
significance: First described from a soldier's skin lesions; long mistaken for a protozoan before its fungal nature was confirmed.

name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
significance: Long classified as a protozoan; genetic evidence in the 1980s reclassified it as a fungus.

name: Rhizopus stolonifer
significance: Common black bread mold; classic model for studying fungal spore dispersal.

name: Claviceps purpurea
discoverer: described in agricultural texts from antiquity; formally named
significance: The ergot fungus, whose alkaloids caused historic poisoning epidemics and later inspired LSD research.

name: Neurospora crassa
discoverer: Bernard Dodge (isolation); George Beadle and Edward Tatum (genetics)
significance: Beadle and Tatum's work on this mold established the "one gene, one enzyme" hypothesis.

name: Schizosaccharomyces pombe
significance: Isolated from East African millet beer; became a key model organism for cell-cycle research.

name: Ustilago maydis
significance: The corn smut fungus, later a model for studying fungal plant pathogenesis and DNA repair.

name: Plasmodium falciparum
significance: First observation of a protozoan parasite as the cause of a human disease, malaria.

name: Plasmodium vivax
significance: Golgi linked fever cycles to the parasite's synchronized blood-stage reproduction.

name: Entamoeba histolytica
significance: First protozoan shown to cause dysentery, isolated from a patient in St. Petersburg.

name: Giardia lamblia
significance: Observed by Leeuwenhoek in his own diarrheal stool, one of the earliest protozoans ever described.

name: Trypanosoma brucei
significance: Identified as the cause of nagana in cattle, later linked to African sleeping sickness.

name: Trypanosoma cruzi
significance: Uniquely, Chagas described the parasite, vector, and disease in a single publication.

name: Toxoplasma gondii
significance: First observed in a North African rodent, the gundi, giving the parasite its name.

name: Leishmania donovani
significance: Independently identified by both researchers as the cause of visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar).

name: Trichomonas vaginalis
significance: One of the earliest human protozoan parasites described using early microscopy.

name: Balantidium coli
significance: Identified in patients with severe diarrhea; remains the only ciliate known to infect humans.

name: Naegleria fowleri
significance: Identified as the cause of a rare, often fatal brain infection from freshwater exposure.

name: Paramecium caudatum
significance: One of the first ciliates ever observed under a microscope; later a foundational genetics model organism.

name: Euglena gracilis
discoverer: early microscopists; formally named by Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg
significance: Its dual plant and animal-like features made it central to early debates over the boundary between kingdoms.

name: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
significance: Became a leading model organism for photosynthesis and flagellar biology research.

name: Chlorella vulgaris
significance: First microalga isolated in pure culture, later studied intensively for photosynthesis research.

name: Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina)
discoverer: described from African and Mexican lakes by 19th-century botanists
significance: Long harvested as a traditional food source before being studied as a nutrient-dense cyanobacterium.

name: Volvox globator
significance: Its rolling colonial spheres were among the first complex microscopic life forms ever documented.

name: Tobacco mosaic virus
significance: Ivanovsky showed the agent passed through filters that trapped bacteria; Beijerinck named it a "contagium vivum fluidum" in 1898, founding virology.

name: Bacteriophage (d'Herelle's phage)
significance: Coined the term "bacteriophage" after observing viruses that kill bacteria, later central to molecular biology.

name: Influenza A virus
discoverer: Wilson Smith; Christopher Andrewes; Patrick Laidlaw
significance: First isolation of a human influenza virus, using ferrets as an animal model.

name: Poliovirus
significance: Demonstrated poliomyelitis was caused by a filterable virus by transmitting it to monkeys.

name: Measles virus
significance: First successful isolation of the virus in tissue culture, enabling later vaccine development.

name: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1)
significance: Isolated from a lymph node biopsy, identifying the retrovirus that causes AIDS.

name: Hepatitis B virus
significance: Grew out of Blumberg's discovery of the "Australia antigen," later identified as the viral surface protein.

name: Ebola virus
discoverer: international team led by Peter Piot
significance: Identified during simultaneous outbreaks near the Ebola River, giving the virus its name.

name: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)
significance: Sequenced within weeks of the first reported cluster of pneumonia cases, enabling rapid global response.

name: Human papillomavirus 16 (HPV16)
significance: Zur Hausen's identification of high-risk HPV types in cervical cancer earned the 2008 Nobel Prize.

name: Deinococcus pantiae
discoverer: National Centre for Cell Science research team, India
location: Schirmacher Oasis, Queen Maud Land, Antarctica
significance: A UV- and vancomycin-resistant extremophile isolated from Antarctic lake sediment in 2026, named in honor of pioneering oceanographer Dr. Aditi Pant.
